Rashi on Niddah 36b:10:1.hebrew: כל שחל קישויה - לאו לשון התחלה הוא, אלא הכי קאמר: כל שקשתה בשלישי, אפי' שעה אחת בליל כניסת שלישי, אפילו כל היום כולו בשופי, ושפתה מליל ד' שעה אחת להשלמת מעת לעת — אין זו יולדת בזוב, דבעינן שופי כל יום ג' המביאה לידי זבה:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:10:1.english: Any [case] where her labor pains occur - It is not an expression of beginning; rather, this is what it is saying: Any [woman] who had labor pains on the third [day] — even [for] one hour on the night of the entrance of the third [day] — even [if she was] the entire day in relief, and she was in relief from the night of the fourth [day] for one hour to complete a twenty-four-hour period, this [woman] is not one who gives birth in [a state of] zov, for we require relief for the entire third day, which brings her to [the status of] zava.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:13:1.hebrew: וכי יזוב זוב - זוב משמע זוב מ"מ, ואפי' באונס:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:13:1.english: And if [a woman] has an issue (zov) - [The word] zov implies a discharge in any case, even [when it occurs] due to circumstances beyond [her] control.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:14:1.english: As there is [a period of] purity after it - [The] blood of purity.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:15:1.english: And [an emission due to] circumstances beyond [her] control in a woman we do not find - That [it is] pure.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:17:1.hebrew: זובה - דם יהיה זובה, ובנדה משתעי, דפרשה ראשונה נאמרה בנדה ושניה בזבה, כדכתיב בשניה: בלא עת נדתה:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:17:1.english: Her issue - [Referring to the verse:] "blood shall be her issue" [Leviticus 15:19], and it speaks of a niddah [menstruating woman], for the first section was stated regarding a niddah and the second regarding a zavah [woman with a flux], as it is written in the second [section]: "outside the time of her menstruation" [Leviticus 15:25].

Rashi on Niddah 36b:17:2.hebrew: ולא מחמת ולד - אלמה אמרינן לעיל: בימי נדה, נדה:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:17:2.english: But not due to [her] child - Why, then, did we say above [that] during the days of niddah, [she is a] niddah?

Rashi on Niddah 36b:19:1.english: She shall remain [in] the blood of purity - For [Scripture] should have written, "And sixty days and six days, blood of purity."

Rashi on Niddah 36b:19:2.english: That is like this - That her blood is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:19:3.hebrew: ואיזו זו - כלומר, היכא משכחת זיבה טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:19:3.english: And which [is] this - That is to say, where do you find pure ziva?

Rashi on Niddah 36b:19:4.hebrew: זו קושי בימי זיבה - דסמיך אדכתיב דמה, מחמת עצמה ולא מחמת ולד:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:19:4.english: This is [the case of] labor pains during the days of ziva - Because [Reish Lakish] relies on that which is written: "her blood" — [meaning] due to herself, and not due to a child.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:1.hebrew: המקשה - וראתה דם, הרי זו נדה. ובגמרא פריך ומתרץ לה:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:1.english: She who experiences [labor] pains - and [she] saw blood, behold she is a niddah. And in the Gemara, it raises an objection and resolves it.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:2.english: She experienced [labor] pains - Because of [the] child.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:3.hebrew: ג' ימים בתוך אחד עשר יום - שבין נדה לנדה, וראתה כל שלשתן הימים רצופין:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:3.english: Three days within eleven days - [That are] between one menstrual period and the next, and she saw [blood on] all three days consecutively.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:4.english: And she rested - From her pain.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:5.english: A twenty-four-hour period - On the fourth [day].

Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:6.hebrew: וילדה - איגלאי מילתא דדמים שראתה לא באו מחמת ולד, הלכך הרי זו יולדת בזוב. אבל אם לא שפתה סמוך ללידתה, כל דמים שראתה מחמת ולד הוא, ורחמנא טהרינהו מזיבה, דכתיב: "זוב דמה" — דמה מחמת עצמה, ולא דמה מחמת ולד:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:1:6.english: And she gave birth - [Thereby] the matter is revealed that the blood she saw did not come on account of the fetus; therefore, she is [considered] one who gives birth as a zava. However, if she did not have a respite [from labor pains] close to her childbirth, all the blood she saw is [considered to have come] on account of the fetus, and the Merciful One declared it pure from [the status of] ziva, as it is written: "the flow of her blood" [Leviticus 15:25] — her blood [that comes] on account of herself, and not her blood [that comes] on account of a fetus.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:21:1.hebrew: ואפי' בשופי - ואפי' הפסיק שופי בין קושי ללידה, נימא טהורה הואיל ודם בקושי בא:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:21:1.english: And even in [a state of] resting - Even if [a period of] resting intervened between [the] labor pains and childbirth, we would say [that] she is pure, since the blood came during labor pains.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:22:1.english: In accordance with [the opinion of] Rav - [That she is] a niddah for that day.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:22:2.hebrew: צנעיה - הסתר אותו דבר, אמור לו שיחזור בו, דטהור לגמרי:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:22:2.english: Hide it - Conceal that matter; tell him to retract [his ruling], for [it] is completely pure.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:22:3.hebrew: גרייה - ברי"ש. כלומר, גרור ומשוך אותו בדברי טעם וראיות שיחזור בו:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:22:3.english: Garyei - With a reish. That is to say, drag and draw him with words of reason and proofs so that he will retract [his ruling].

Rashi on Niddah 36b:22:4.english: Gadyei - Cut him off with excommunication, as [in the verse] (Daniel 4): "Cut down [godu] the tree."

Rashi on Niddah 36b:23:1.english: He would have told me - For I am his student.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:23:2.english: He excommunicated him - He placed him under a ban.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:2:1.hebrew: לילה ויום - דאם שפתה בחצי יום שלישי וילדה יום רביעי, דשפתה מעת לעת, אין זו שופי, אלא אם כן שפתה לילה ויום שלאחר הלילה, כלילי שבת ויומו:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:2:1.english: A night and a day - For if she rested in the middle of the third day [Tuesday] and gave birth on the fourth day [Wednesday], so that she rested for a twenty-four-hour period, this is not [considered a valid] respite, unless she rested a night and the day following the night, like Shabbat evening and its day.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:2:2.hebrew: ששפתה מן הצער ולא מן הדם - דאע"ג דחזיא דם, הוי שופי:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:2:2.english: Where she rested from the pain and not from the blood - [Meaning] that even though she sees blood, it is [considered] a respite.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:3:1.english: How long is her labor pain - [Such] that she does not come to [a state of] ziva through any blood that she sees.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:3:2.hebrew: אפילו ארבעים או חמשים יום - אם לא שפתה יום אחד סמוך ללידה, לא אתיא לידי זיבה ולא הויא יולדת בזוב:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:3:2.english: Even forty or fifty days - If she did not have a respite [from labor pains] for one day close to childbirth, she does not come to [a state of] ziva, and she is not [considered] a woman who gives birth in [a state of] ziva.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:3:3.hebrew: דיה חדשה - דיה אם נטהר את הקושי חדש אחד, היינו תשיעי. אבל קשתה שלשה בתוך י"א ימי זיבה בחדש השמיני, ואפי' מקשה והולכת כל תשיעי, הרי זו יולדת בזוב מחמת שלשה ימים של שמיני:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:3:3.english: Her month is sufficient for her - It is sufficient for her if we declare the labor pains pure [for] one month, that is, the ninth [month]. However, [if] she had labor pains [for] three [days] within the eleven days of ziva in the eighth month, even [if] she continues having labor pains all of the ninth [month], she is a woman who gives birth in [a state of] zov on account of the three days of the eighth [month].

Rashi on Niddah 36b:4:1.hebrew: אטו כל המקשה נדה היא - אילו קשתה בימי זיבה, מי הויא נדה? והא אין נדות בימי זוב:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:4:1.english: Is this to say that any [woman] who experiences labor pains is a menstruating woman - If she experienced labor pains during the days of ziva, would she be a menstruating woman? But surely there is no menstruation during the days of ziva.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב נדה ליומא - וה"ק, המקשה ורואה דם בימי זיבה, אע"ג דלא אתיא ביה לידי זיבה, מיהו באותו היום אסורה לשמש, אבל לערב טובלת, ואינה צריכה לשמור יום כנגד יום, דרחמנא טהריה לדם קושי:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:5:1.english: Rav said: A menstruating woman for [one] day - And this is what he is saying: [A woman] who is in labor and sees blood during the days of ziva, even though she does not come through it to [a state of] ziva, nevertheless on that day she is forbidden to engage in marital relations; however, in the evening she immerses, and she does not need to observe a [clean] day corresponding to [the] day [of bleeding], for the Merciful One declared the blood of labor pure.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:5:2.hebrew: ושמואל אמר - אף צריכה לשמור יום כנגד יום מדרבנן, דחיישינן שמא תשפה, ונמצא שלא היה דם קושי מחמת ולד, ונמצא משמש עם זבה קטנה דאורייתא, וענוש כרת:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:5:2.english: And Shmuel said - [She is] also required to observe a day for a day by rabbinic law, for we are concerned lest she rest [from labor], and it would turn out that the blood of [her] labor-pangs was not due to the child, and it would turn out [that her husband] has intercourse with a minor zava by Torah law, and is liable to karet.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:6:1.english: Is nothing - And even on that same day she [may] engage in marital relations.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:7:1.english: During the days of menstruation - During the days that are fit for menstruation.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:7:2.hebrew: נדה - דקושי לא טהריה רחמנא אלא מזיבה, אבל מנדה לא טהריה, כדאמרי' לקמן:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:7:2.english: A menstruating woman - For the Merciful One did not declare [bleeding due to] labor pains pure except from ziva, but from niddah He did not declare it pure, as we say below.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:7:3.hebrew: בימי זיבה - בתוך אחד עשר יום, טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:7:3.english: During the days of ziva - Within [the] eleven days, [she is] pure.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:7:4.english: And it is taught - [This is said] in a declarative tone.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:8:1.hebrew: ושפתה - שנים, מן הצער ולא מן הדם:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:8:1.english: And she rested - [for] two [days], from the pain and not from the blood.

Rashi on Niddah 36b:8:2.hebrew: הרי זו יולדת בזוב - אם ראתה כל שלש, הואיל ושופי סמוך ללידה, נמצא דם הקושי שלא מחמת ולד:
Rashi on Niddah 36b:8:2.english: This [woman] is one who gives birth as a zava - If she saw [blood on] all three [days], since [there was] relief [from labor pains] close to childbirth, the blood of the labor pains turns out [to be] not on account of the child.

Tosafot on Niddah 36b:19:1.hebrew: ואימא קושי בימי נדה - ור"ל ס"ד דמסתבר טפי לאוקומיה בזיבה, משום דאשכחן זב אונס דטהור הוא:
Tosafot on Niddah 36b:19:1.english: "But say [that this is] labor pains during the days of niddah" - And Reish Lakish thought that it is more reasonable to establish it [as referring] to zivah, because we find [regarding] a zav [that an emission due to] an external cause is pure.

Tosafot on Niddah 36b:22:1.hebrew: גדייה - פרש"י דרב אסי טעה בין רי"ש לדלי"ת. ואין נראה, אלא נראה דאיהו אמר ליה "גדייה" בדלי"ת רפה, כלומר: משכהו בדברי טעם עד שיחזור, כמו (שמות יב) "משכו" דמתרגמינן "נגודו", וכמו (ב"ב דף יג.) "גוד או איגוד"; והוא סבר "גדייה" בדגש, כמו "גודו אילנא":
Tosafot on Niddah 36b:22:1.english: Gadyei - Rashi explained that Rav Asi erred between a reish and a dalet. But [this] does not appear [correct]; rather, it appears that he [Rav] said to him "gedyei" with a soft dalet [i.e., without a dagesh] — that is to say, draw him with words of reason until he retracts, like [the verse] (Exodus 12[:21]) "Draw out [mishkhu]," which we translate [in Aramaic as] "negudu," and like (Bava Batra 13a) "Gud o igud" [lit. draw or I will draw]; whereas he [Rav Asi] thought [he meant] "gadyei" with a dagesh [meaning cut off/excommunicate], like [the verse] "Hew down the tree [godu ilana]."

Tosafot on Niddah 36b:2:1.hebrew: כלילי שבת ויומו - קים ליה לרבי יהושע דאם לא שפתה לילה ויום, אע"פ ששפתה מעת לעת, מחמת ולד היה:
Tosafot on Niddah 36b:2:1.english: Like Shabbat evening and its day - Rabbi Yehoshua was certain that if she did not rest [from pain for] a night and a day, even if she rested for a twenty-four-hour period, [it] was due to the fetus.

Tosafot on Niddah 36b:5:1.hebrew: נדה ליומא - נראה דאף לבעלה לא חיישינן שמא תשפה, דאזלינן בתר רוב נשים מקשות דאינן שפות לילה ויום; דהא עובדא דשילא בר אבינא נראה דלבעלה הוי ולא לטהרות:
Tosafot on Niddah 36b:5:1.english: A menstruating woman for a day - It appears that even with respect to her husband we are not concerned lest she rest [from labor], for we follow the majority of women in labor, who do not rest [for] a night and a day; for [regarding] the incident of Shila bar Avina, it appears that it was with respect to her husband and not with respect to purities [teharot].

Tosafot on Niddah 36b:8:1.hebrew: או ששפתה וקשתה וחזרה ושפתה - כדי נסבה, דהא מרישא שמעינן לה, דקתני "קשתה שנים ושפתה יום אחד", וכ"ש הא דטמאה. וכן בסיפא לא היה צריך למתני "קשתה ושפתה וקשתה", כיון דתנא "שפתה שנים וקשתה יום אחד" דטהורה. אי נמי, אתא לאשמועינן אע"ג דלא קשתה כל יום הסמוך ללידה אלא מקצתו; וכן ברישא בכי האי גוונא:
Tosafot on Niddah 36b:8:1.english: Or if she rested [from labor] and experienced [labor] pains and again rested [from labor] - It [the baraita] cited this incidentally, for we already learn it from the first clause, which teaches "she experienced [labor] pains for two [days] and rested [from labor] for one day," and all the more so [is it obvious in] this [case] that she is impure [as a zava]. And similarly in the latter clause, it was not necessary to teach "she experienced [labor] pains and rested [from labor] and experienced [labor] pains," since it taught "she rested [from labor] for two [days] and experienced [labor] pains for one day" that she is pure. Alternatively, it comes to teach us [that the ruling applies] even though she did not experience [labor] pains for the entire day adjacent to the birth, but rather part of it; and similarly in the first clause in such a case.
